## Proof

**Setup.** Let $V = k^{n+1}$. The Grassmannian $G(1, n+1)$ parametrizes 1-dimensional subspaces of $V$, hence $G(1,n+1) \cong \mathbb{P}^n_k = \mathbb{P}(V)$. On $\mathbb{P}(V)$ we have the **tautological exact sequence**:

$$0 \to \mathscr{S} \xrightarrow{\;\iota\;} V \otimes \mathscr{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n} \xrightarrow{\;\pi\;} \mathscr{Q} \to 0 \tag{1}$$

where $\mathscr{S} = \mathscr{O}(-1)$ is the tautological subbundle (fiber at $[v]$ is the line $kv \subset V$) and $\mathscr{Q}$ is the tautological quotient bundle of rank $n$.

---

**Step 1: Dualize the tautological sequence.** Since all terms in (1) are locally free, dualizing is exact:

$$0 \to \mathscr{Q}^\vee \xrightarrow{\;\pi^\vee\;} V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n} \xrightarrow{\;\iota^\vee\;} \mathscr{O}(1) \to 0 \tag{2}$$

using $\mathscr{S}^\vee = \mathscr{O}(-1)^\vee = \mathscr{O}(1)$ and $(V\otimes\mathscr{O})^\vee = V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}$.

---

**Step 2: Tensor with $\mathscr{O}(-1)$.** Tensoring (2) with the line bundle $\mathscr{O}(-1)$ (which is locally free, hence exact):

$$0 \to \mathscr{Q}^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \to V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \xrightarrow{\;\iota^\vee \otimes \mathrm{id}\;} \mathscr{O}(1)\otimes\mathscr{O}(-1) \to 0 \tag{3}$$

Since $\mathscr{O}(1)\otimes\mathscr{O}(-1) \cong \mathscr{O}$, this becomes:

$$0 \to \mathscr{Q}^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \to V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \xrightarrow{\;\delta\;} \mathscr{O} \to 0 \tag{3'}$$

where $\delta = \iota^\vee \otimes \mathrm{id}$ is the **contraction map**: it is the map induced by the tautological inclusion $\iota: \mathscr{O}(-1) \hookrightarrow V\otimes\mathscr{O}$, viewed via the canonical identification
$$\mathrm{Hom}(\mathscr{O}(-1),\, V\otimes\mathscr{O}) \;\cong\; \mathrm{Hom}(V^\vee\otimes\mathscr{O}(-1),\, \mathscr{O}) = H^0\!\big(V^\vee\otimes\mathscr{O}(-1)^\vee\big).$$

Concretely, on the open set $U_i = \{x_i \neq 0\}$ with trivialization $\mathscr{O}(-1)|_{U_i} \cong \mathscr{O}_{U_i}$, the map $\delta$ sends a section $(f_0, \dots, f_n) \in \mathscr{O}(-1)^{\oplus(n+1)}$ to $\sum_j x_j f_j / x_i$, which is the standard contraction.

---

**Step 3: Identify with the Euler exact sequence.** The **Euler exact sequence** on $\mathbb{P}^n_k$ is:

$$0 \to \Omega_{\mathbb{P}^n/k} \to V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \xrightarrow{\;\delta\;} \mathscr{O} \to 0 \tag{4}$$

where the map $\delta: V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1) \to \mathscr{O}$ is precisely the contraction map arising from the tautological subbundle $\mathscr{O}(-1) \hookrightarrow V \otimes \mathscr{O}$. This is the standard construction of the Euler sequence: it is obtained from the surjection $V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O} \to \mathscr{O}(1)$ (dual of the tautological inclusion) by tensoring with $\mathscr{O}(-1)$, and its kernel is $\Omega_{\mathbb{P}^n/k}$ by the theory of the Euler sequence (equivalently, by the conormal sequence for the projection $V\setminus\{0\} \to \mathbb{P}(V)$ modulo the $\mathbb{G}_m$-action).

---

**Step 4: Conclude the isomorphism.** Sequences (3') and (4) are **the same short exact sequence**: they share the same middle term $V^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1)$, the same right term $\mathscr{O}$, and—crucially—the **same map** $\delta$ (the contraction map from the tautological inclusion) between them. Therefore their kernels are canonically identified:

$$\Omega_{\mathbb{P}^n/k} \;=\; \ker(\delta) \;=\; \mathscr{Q}^\vee \otimes \mathscr{O}(-1).$$

Finally, using $\mathscr{S} = \mathscr{O}(-1)$ and the standard identity $\mathscr{Q}^\vee \otimes \mathscr{S} = \mathscr{H}om(\mathscr{Q}, \mathscr{S})$ (since $\mathscr{Q}$ is locally free):

$$\boxed{\Omega_{\mathbb{P}^n_k/k} \;\cong\; \mathscr{H}om(\mathscr{Q},\, \mathscr{S}).}$$

This isomorphism is **canonical**: it requires no choice of basis or trivialization, arising entirely from the tautological exact sequence and the canonical construction of the Euler sequence from it. $\blacksquare$
